title: The Creepy Legacy of the Hotel Cecil
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the Hotel Cecil in downtown Los Angeles, its decline from a 1920s middle-class hotel near Skid Row into a site of many unnatural deaths, and the 2013 disappearance and death of Canadian traveler Elisa Lam, whose body was found in a rooftop water tank. They cover the elevator surveillance video, the police findings on her untreated bipolar disorder and medications, the water tank discovery, Josh Dean's investigation, and the debunking of internet conspiracy theories. Also covered: serial killers Richard Ramirez and Jack Unterweger who stayed at the hotel, a Stuff You Should Know board game announcement, and a listener mail about the Y2K Unix problem.
topics: Stuff You Should Know board game

segments.title: Opening banter and board game announcement
segments.summary: The hosts give a trigger warning, announce the Stuff You Should Know Trivial Pursuit board game made with Hasbro, and introduce the episode.
topics: Stuff You Should Know board game

segments.title: Caveats on myths and Elisa Lam's mental illness
segments.summary: The hosts say internet myths and conspiracy theories about the case are false and disrespectful, since Elisa Lam had untreated serious mental illness.

segments.title: Hotel Cecil history and Stay on Main
segments.summary: The Hotel Cecil opened in the 1920s in downtown Los Angeles near a rail station, with Beaux-Arts architecture. It was later rebranded Stay on Main, with a separate lobby and renovated floors, and was planned for renovation before COVID.

segments.title: Skid Row and the hotel's decline
segments.summary: The hotel's surroundings became Skid Row after the stock market crash and Great Depression. Falling guest numbers led to lower rates and neglect, and the hotel became a last-resort lodging for people with addictions and in sex work.

segments.title: Unnatural deaths at the Cecil
segments.summary: The hosts list many deaths at the hotel, including suicides, jumps, murders, and a 1930s-era incident where Pauline Oughten landed on a passerby. A former manager claimed at least eighty deaths during her tenure, though documented cases are fewer. A Netflix documentary by Joe Berlinger is mentioned.

segments.title: Richard Ramirez and Jack Unterweger at the Cecil
segments.summary: Richard Ramirez, the Night Stalker, stayed at the hotel and was caught by an East LA mob in the 1980s. Austrian serial killer Jack Unterweger later stayed there while posing as a true crime journalist and killed sex workers.

segments.title: Elisa Lam's arrival and disappearance
segments.summary: Elisa Lam, a 20-year-old Canadian traveling alone up the West Coast, stayed at Stay on Main in a hostel-style room for about $75 a night. She was due to check out February 1, 2013 and did not call her parents, and was last seen shopping for books. Two men handed her a large box in front of the hotel.

segments.title: Police search and elevator video
segments.summary: Police searched the hotel and found her belongings in storage. The public took little notice until the elevator surveillance video was released, showing Lam acting strangely, hiding in a corner and gesturing into the hallway. The hosts discuss editing claims and interpretations.

segments.title: Body found in water tank and mental health findings
segments.summary: A maintenance worker, Santiago Lopez, found Lam's nude body in one of the rooftop water tanks after complaints about water pressure and odor. Police found she had been off her medications for bipolar disorder and depression. The hosts discuss the rooftop access via fire escape and the ladder, and Josh Dean's reporting.

segments.title: Listener mail on the Y2K Unix problem
segments.summary: A listener, citing Alan Chalker, explains the Unix Y2K-style rollover problem on January 19, 2038, when time counted from the 1970 epoch runs out, and notes that newer systems have fixed it.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and give contact information.
